scope: Characterize the FFXIV 1.x event/cutscene/NPC-dialog subsystem opcodes using the receiver_opcode_map_inbound classification and the FUN_004D8860 event-family sub-dispatcher case table. Identify which event opcodes are catalog-covered through existing chains, which are draft-staged, and which need new catalog entries.

method.step7: Identified BCS-Y-0426..0434 as the cataloged c2s 0x012D EventStartPacket emit chain (client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric') - the c2s EventStart side is fully attributed

method.step9: Identified the Lua-engine callback registry (docs/lua-engine-callback-registry.md, BCS-Y-0397..0403) where _onTalkEvent / _onPushEvent / _onPreEvent / _onPostEvent etc. are fired by C++ via FUN_00447260 + FUN_00CC7A90

subsystem_overview.summary: FFXIV 1.x's event subsystem is the engine's mechanism for staging NPC dialog, cutscene playback, push-trigger interactions, talk events, and short-lived interactive sequences. It is bidirectional: the client EMITS c2s EventStart (0x012D) / EventUpdate (0x012E) packets with eventName + luaParams to declare intent, and the server REPLIES with the s2c control opcodes (KickEvent / RunEventFunction / EndEvent / SetXxxEventCondition variants) that drive the client-side event state machine and pick which Lua handlers fire.
subsystem_overview.c2s_side: One opcode (0x012D EventStart) carries the entire c2s vocabulary via the eventName/luaParams strings (per client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric'). EventStart is built by MapEventStartPacketBuilder_FUN_00776760 (BCS-Y-0426), staged by 5 wrappers (BCS-Y-0427..0431), and sent through FUN_004D6D30 -> FUN_004E0240 -> FUN_00DAE010. The 0x012E EventUpdate pair is bidirectional with 0x012E SetTalkEventCondition (s2c), creating a known opcode collision.
subsystem_overview.s2c_side: 13 event-related opcodes split into 3 dispatch tiers: (a) Tier-A direct receivers for SetEmote / SetCommand-named / SetPushCircle / SetPushFan / SetPushTriggerBox / SetTalk / SetNotice (each is a *EventConditionReceiver class with its own RTTI - some route via Pattern B vftable[9] cases in the FUN_004DC690 high-switch); (b) Tier-D event-family dispatch via FUN_004D8860 (BCS-Y-0280) for KickEvent / RunEventFunction / EndEvent / SetEventStatus - each chain is FUN_004DC690 -> FUN_004D8860 -> case trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[slot] -> Receiver::Receive; (c) the Deferred Event-Condition scheduler (BCS-Y-0470..0476), where Talk/Push leaves fire callbacks after receivers store callback records. NoticeBlock/NoticeNonBlock leaf slot +0x28 is a no-op.
subsystem_overview.cutscene_side: Cutscene playback is handled via the Control::CutScene class (existing BCS-Y entries: vtable, slot2 lua_api_dispatcher_multi_firer, and 5 lua_firers _setFilename / _loadCutScene / _play / _replay / _skip). Cutscene callbacks (onPreCutSceneCancel slot 38, onPostCutSceneCancel slot 39, onCutScenePreview NullActorImpl slot 36) are LuaActorImpl::vftable slots. Cutscene PLAYBACK is local-only; cutscenes are STARTED by EventStart 0x012D with a cutscene-shaped eventName/luaParams payload that the script-side then triggers via _play. CutScene_PlayExecuteParametersAdapter_FUN_006FB830 and CutScene_ReplayExecuteParametersAdapter_FUN_006F11B0 (existing BCS-Y) are the c++ adapters that script-side _play / _replay calls route through
subsystem_overview.no_dedicated_dialog_opcode: The 1.x client has NO dedicated 'DialogBox' / 'NpcMenu' / 'YesNoMenu' opcode. NPC dialog rendering is a CLIENT-SIDE Lua-script concern driven by the SetTalkEventCondition (0x012E s2c) + RunEventFunction (0x0130 s2c) + EndEvent (0x0131 s2c) sequence. The script-side NpcBaseClass.lua / DirectorBaseClass.lua _onTalkEvent / _onTalkRequest handlers parse the LuaParams in RunEventFunction packets and call into the DesktopWidget UI (_appendLogPool / _appendMessagePool for system messages, message-box / menu APIs for dialog rendering)

event_opcode_table.name: EventStart (MapEventStartPacket)
event_opcode_table.purpose: Client declares event intent (talk start, push trigger, command exec, cutscene init, combat command). Carries eventName + luaParams. The single c2s opcode for all event/intent emission per client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric'.
event_opcode_table.dispatchChain: Lua _doServerOnTalk/_callServerOnTalk/etc -> FUN_0075E230 EventStartServerCallWrapper (BCS-Y-0427) OR FUN_0075E1C0/0089E0D0 raw wrappers (BCS-Y-0428) OR FUN_0075E3A0 route wrapper (BCS-Y-0429) OR FUN_0075E510 follow-up wrapper (BCS-Y-0430) -> FUN_00776760 MapEventStartPacketBuilder (BCS-Y-0426) -> FUN_004D6D30 zone gate -> FUN_004E0240 Tier-C forwarder -> FUN_00DAE010 terminal send
event_opcode_table.notes: Client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric' section's central opcode. Only the c2s emit path is wired in the FFXIV 1.x client binary.

event_opcode_table.name: EventUpdate (c2s) / SetTalkEventCondition (s2c)
event_opcode_table.purpose: c2s: client follow-up update during a running event (menu selection, dialog confirm, mid-cutscene state). s2c: server tells client to install a talk-event condition on an actor (cast to NpcBase).
event_opcode_table.dispatchChainS2C: FUN_004D8860 case 0x12E -> FUN_00574FD0 trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[50] (FUN_00759FE0 cataloged? slot 50 not explicitly in BCS-Y-0092) -> ... -> SetTalkEventConditionReceiver::Receive (slot1Fn FUN_0089df60) -> __RTDynamicCast(ActorBase->NpcBase) -> install talk condition. ATTENTION: receiver_opcode_map maps 0x012E to SetTalkEventConditionReceiver, but the pattern-d-subdispatcher pass maps case 0x12E to LuaActorImpl slot 50, which is in the noop/stateless range per BCS-Y-0092. The actual receiver dispatch may use a different mechanism than this case path; a follow-up walk is required.
event_opcode_table.dispatchChainC2S: Lua menu/dialog response -> _doServerOn[Talk/...] family -> reuses the 0x012D EventStart emit chain? Or a separate builder? OPEN QUESTION - the c2s EventUpdate emitter has NOT been identified statically (the combat action c2s findings pass focused on 0x012D).
event_opcode_table.notes: Bidirectional opcode collision - the third one found in the catalog after 0x01DD and 0x0F (CharaMakeOperation vs GameLoginOperation). Different payload shapes per direction (c2s 0x78 update vs s2c 0x48 condition install).

event_opcode_table.name: KickEvent (KickEventPacket)
event_opcode_table.purpose: Server kicks off an event sequence on an actor (talk / push / notice / emote / etc). Carries triggerActorId + ownerActorId + eventType byte + eventName + luaParams. Drives most NPC interactions.
event_opcode_table.dispatchChain: FUN_004DC690 high-switch (case 0x12F NOT in the high-switch-enumeration pass's table - falls into FUN_004D8860's path via case 0x12F) -> FUN_00575030 trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[56] (FUN_0076C0D0) -> KickClientOrderEventReceiver::Receive (5-slot vtable; real Receive at slot 2 = FUN_0089E450 NOT slot1Fn) -> FUN_0089F180 (KickEvent parser, 289 bytes) -> per kick_receiver_offset_map.md: receiver[+0x80] = 1 iff event_type byte == 0x05 (noticeEvent tag); conditionally seeds FUN_0089E200 (92 bytes) to set LuaParamsContainer+0x14 = 1
event_opcode_table.chain: BCS-Y-0280 case 0x12F (proposed BCS-Y-0538 draft = KickClientOrderEventReceiverTrampoline_Case0x12F_FUN_00575030, LuaActorImpl slot 56 trampoline)
event_opcode_table.notes: Deep-decoded. The `+0x5c` actor flag gate is the legendary silent-drop trigger - the kick is suppressed if actor[+0x5c] != 0 at receive time. KickClientOrderEventReceiver is a 5-slot vtable where slot1Fn is the New() factory NOT the Receive - per docs/receiver_classes_inventory.md, the real Receive is slot 2 (FUN_0089E450). client_receivers.json's slot1Fn field is misleading for 5/6-slot receivers (see local memory ledger reference-receiver-vtable-layouts.md).

event_opcode_table.name: RunEventFunction (RunEventFunctionPacket)
event_opcode_table.purpose: Server tells client to run a specific Lua function on an actor during an active event. Carries triggerActorId + ownerActorId + eventType + eventName + functionName + luaParams. This is how server passes 'show this dialog text' / 'play this cutscene' / 'open this menu' to the client mid-event. Probably the dominant 'NPC says X' delivery mechanism.
event_opcode_table.dispatchChain: FUN_004D8860 case 0x130 -> FUN_00575040 trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[57] (FUN_0076C220) -> StartServerOrderEventFunctionReceiver::Receive (5-slot vtable; real Receive at slot 2)
event_opcode_table.chain: BCS-Y-0280 case 0x130 (proposed BCS-Y-0539 draft = StartServerOrderEventFunctionReceiverTrampoline_Case0x130_FUN_00575040, LuaActorImpl slot 57)
luaCallbacks: server-passed function name; could be ANY method on the targeted actor's class
event_opcode_table.notes: Deep-decoded. eventName at offset 9; functionName at offset 0x29; luaParams at offset 0x49. The 696-byte size suggests dialog text strings can be carried inline (much larger than KickEvent's 0x90).

event_opcode_table.name: EndEvent (EndEventPacket)
event_opcode_table.purpose: Server tells client an event has ended. Carries sourcePlayerActorId + eventOwnerActorID + eventType + eventName and drives native event cleanup without a Lua callback firer in this receiver chain.
event_opcode_table.dispatchChain: FUN_004D8860 case 0x131 -> FUN_00575050 trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[58] (FUN_0076C3B0) -> EndClientOrderEventReceiver slot 2 Receive FUN_0089D200; slot 3 FUN_0089E2D0 performs actor lookup and calls the 102-case FUN_008A13A0 dispatcher.
event_opcode_table.chain: BCS-Y-0280 case 0x131 (proposed BCS-Y-0540 draft = EndClientOrderEventReceiverTrampoline_Case0x131_FUN_00575050, LuaActorImpl slot 58)
event_opcode_table.notes: Deep-decoded. Slot 2 unconditionally writes success. Slot 3 calls the 102-case native end-event dispatcher; no Lua firer appears in this receiver chain. Source: xivl-decomp:docs/event/end-order-event-receiver.md.

event_opcode_table.name: SetEventStatus (SetEventStatusPacket)
event_opcode_table.purpose: Server tells client to enable/disable an event-condition on an NPC actor. Carries enabled flag + type byte + conditionName (max 0x24 bytes).
event_opcode_table.dispatchChain: FUN_004D8860 case 0x136 -> FUN_00574FB0 trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[48] (FUN_00759D20) -> SetEventStatusReceiver::Receive (FUN_0089D860) -> __RTDynamicCast(ActorBase->NpcBase) -> FUN_006E67C0 apply: switches on receiver+0x58 to select a lookup helper, then calls vtable[9] on the looked-up state object. NO chain-key writes (per BCS-Y-0362).
event_opcode_table.chain: BCS-Y-0280 case 0x136 (proposed BCS-Y-0543 draft = SetEventStatusReceiverTrampoline_Case0x136_FUN_00574FB0, LuaActorImpl slot 48)
event_opcode_table.notes: Surprisingly no BCS-Y for the receiver class or slot1Fn. This is a Pattern A1 (RTDynamicCast + dispatch, no null-check guard) receiver. SetEventStatus is the most-emitted event-condition opcode in the corpus - any zone with active event NPCs generates lots of these.

event_opcode_table.name: SetActorNamePacket (SetDisplayName)
event_opcode_table.purpose: Server tells client to update an actor's displayed name. NOT strictly event-family but in the same dispatch range and used during event triggers.
event_opcode_table.dispatchChain: FUN_004D8860 case 0x13D -> FUN_00575100 trampoline -> LuaActorImpl::vftable[62] (FUN_0076C4D0) -> SetDisplayNameReceiver::Receive (FUN_0089D610)

event_opcode_table.notes: Adjacent to the event family. Included here because the pattern-d-subdispatcher pass lists it in the event-family dispatcher's case table.

BUT receiver_opcode_map says 0x016B->SetNoticeEventConditionReceiver (slot1Fn FUN_0089d980). event_opcode_table.purpose: Server installs an 'emote' event condition. Triggers when player performs a specific emote near the actor. Drives the /salute, /wave-style NPC reactions.

RECEIVER MISMATCH: receiver_opcode_map says 0x016C->SetEmoteEventConditionReceiver (slot1Fn FUN_0089d750, non-RTDynamicCast packer). Most likely the receiver is reached via FUN_004DC690 high-switch case 0x16C falling through to vftable[9] (Pattern B) rather than through FUN_004D8860 - the BCS-Y-0527 generic fallthrough mechanism.
event_opcode_table.notes: Conflict between the pattern-d-subdispatcher pass (no-op slot 52) vs receiver_opcode_map (SetEmoteEventConditionReceiver). The likely resolution: FUN_004D8860's path is one of TWO dispatch sites for 0x16C, and the operative one is the FUN_004DC690 Pattern B fallthrough. Opcode 0x17B has dual dispatch paths per PATTERNDSUBD-F4 - 0x16C may be similar.

deferred_event_scheduler_chain.summary: After SetTalk/Push/Notice/Emote event-condition receivers store callback records, the runtime side fires the actual _onTalkEvent/_onPushEvent/_onPreEvent/_onPostEvent leaf callbacks via a native C++ state machine (NOT Lua coroutines per client-architecture 'Deferred event execution uses native C++ state machines').
deferred_event_scheduler_chain.chain: Set*EventCondition receiver -> FUN_0089DB00 (SetPushCircle slot1 example) -> FUN_006F2B70 DeferredEventConditionProducer -> FUN_00CC73B0 (actor/control wrap) -> FUN_0075C4A0 -> FUN_004D9970 (target key touch) + FUN_00445210 (key resolver) + FUN_0058B110 (slot writer) -> 2-slot 0x54-stride callback table BCS-S-0037 EventConditionCallbackSlot
deferred_event_scheduler_chain.execution_side: FUN_00897310 (block) + FUN_008955C0 (non-block walker) check Event::Base vtable+0x1c, then dispatch via FUN_008962C0/FUN_008963F0 pair -> vtable+0x04 wrapper FUN_00897570 -> leaf vtable+0x28 firer (this is where _onTalkEvent / _onPushEvent / _onPushRequest land)
bcsYRefs: BCS-Y-0470..0476 (scheduler chain - per client-architecture 'Deferred event execution uses native C++ state machines')

cutscene_chain.summary: Cutscene playback is local-only. Cutscenes are started by EventStart 0x012D with a cutscene-shaped payload, and the script side calls CutScene class methods (_setFilename, _loadCutScene, _play, _replay, _skip) that route through C++ adapters.
cutscene_chain.no_dedicated_opcode: Confirmed by absence: no cutscene-specific opcode appears in the FUN_004DC690 case table. Cutscene start uses 0x0130 RunEventFunction (where functionName is the cutscene name) or EventStart 0x012D with cutscene luaParams.

npc_dialog_chain.summary: NPC dialog box rendering is ENTIRELY a client-side Lua-script concern with no dedicated wire opcode. The server triggers dialog via RunEventFunction 0x0130 (passing the script-side function name as a string), and the client-side NpcBaseClass.lua _onTalkEvent handler parses luaParams and calls into the DesktopWidget UI APIs to render dialog box / menu / yes-no widgets.
npc_dialog_chain.client_side_dialog_rendering: Per docs/packet-dispatch-map.md, when the player initiates an NPC interaction, the client engine fires npc:_onTalkEvent(player, packet) through _callServerOnTalk_cpp (NpcBaseClass.lua line 446). The C++ binding writes npc[+0x128] = player_actor_id before sending the talk-request packet 0x012D EventStart. The response uses 0x0130 RunEventFunction to select the Lua function, which then calls DesktopWidget log-pool, message-pool, message-box, or menu APIs to render the dialog UI.
npc_dialog_chain.ui_render_chain: The shipped Lua scripts (chara/npc/<area>/<populace>/*.lua) typically: receive _onTalkRequest -> parse luaParams[0] (talk command name) -> dispatch to a per-command handler -> call DesktopWidget UI APIs (_setMessage / _setMessageMenu / _showYesNoMenu / etc.) to render the dialog. Client-driven; server only sees the c2s 0x012D follow-up EventStart with the menu selection result in luaParams

setEventStatus.gates: kind byte must match one of three discriminator constants and the event-name lookup must find a registered entry; either mismatch is a silent no-op.

setNoticeEventCondition.cast: ActorBase -> DirectorBase is a soft cast; success stores in DirectorBase+0x60, failure falls back to ActorBase+0x118.
setNoticeEventCondition.sequencingRisk: A packet received before ScriptBind can register the condition in the ActorBase fallback container rather than the DirectorBase container.

key_findings.title: Event subsystem opcodes are well-mapped but receiver classes mostly lack BCS-Y RTTI entries
key_findings.summary: The 14 event-family receiver classes are all attributed in receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json by RTTI RVA + slot1Fn VA + opcode, but only 3 have actual BCS-Y RTTI entries (KickClientOrderEvent = 0028/0029, StartServerOrderEventFunction = 0030/0031, EndClientOrderEvent = 0032/0033). The other 11 receivers (SetEventStatus, SetDisplayName, SetNoticeEvent, SetEmoteEvent, SetPushCircle/Fan/TriggerBox, SetTalkEvent, SetCommandEvent, plus 2 5-slot Receive method gaps) need BCS-Y class+slot1 entries. This proposes 16 of these (BCS-Y-0684..0699).

key_findings.title: 1.x has NO dedicated NPC dialog / cutscene opcode - both are client-side Lua-rendered
key_findings.summary: Despite the user-visible prominence of NPC dialog boxes and cutscene playback, the 1.x wire protocol has ZERO dedicated opcodes for either. NPC dialog: server sends 0x0130 RunEventFunction with a Lua function name; client-side scripts render the dialog UI via DesktopWidget _appendLogPool / message-box APIs. Cutscene: server sends 0x012D EventStart with cutscene luaParams OR 0x0130 RunEventFunction with the cutscene play function; client-side Control::CutScene Lua bindings (_setFilename / _loadCutScene / _play / _replay / _skip) handle local playback. This is consistent with client-architecture 'Lua N-API setters are client-local by design' (server-authoritative state, client-emits-intent) - dialog rendering is purely a CLIENT presentation concern.

key_findings.title: The pattern-d-subdispatcher pass vs receiver_opcode_map disagreement: 0x16C SetEmote and 0x16B SetNotice route via no-op LuaActorImpl slots
key_findings.summary: FUN_004D8860's case table maps 0x16B->LuaActorImpl::vftable[51] (FUN_00574FE0, a no-op stub via BCS-Y-0092 categorization) and 0x16C->slot 52 (FUN_00759E10, confirmed 3-byte no-op stub per the event-family-sibling-findings pass). YET receiver_opcode_map confirms these opcodes have real receivers (SetNoticeEventConditionReceiver / SetEmoteEventConditionReceiver). Resolution hypothesis: the actual dispatch path is FUN_004DC690's Pattern B fallthrough (BCS-Y-0527 generic vftable[9]) - not FUN_004D8860's event-family path. This is the dual-path scenario flagged for 0x17B (PATTERNDSUBD-F4). 0x16B/0x16C likely have similar dual paths.

key_findings.title: 0x166 SetCommandEventConditionReceiver entry in receiver_opcode_map is wrong - 0x166 is a SendLogReceiver subcategory
key_findings.summary: receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json lists 0x0166 SetCommandEventConditionReceiver (RTTI 0xc5737c, slot1Fn FUN_0089D4F0). But the SendLogReceiver demux confirms 0x0166 is the SendLogReceiver subcategory 'GameMessageWithoutActor1' with ctor handler FUN_008A0A60 (shared with 0x15C subcategory CustomSender1). The 20-opcode fallthrough cluster 0x157..0x16A all routes to SendLogReceiver via FUN_004D8860 case slot 63 (FUN_00575E30 wrapper). The receiver does exist (it has its own RTTI at 0xc5737c with slot1Fn FUN_0089D4F0); the wire opcode mapping in receiver_opcode_map is wrong. SetCommandEventCondition's real wire opcode (if any) needs re-identification. **This is a catalog data-quality finding worth a separate phase to clean up.**

key_findings.title: EventStart 0x012D is the universal c2s entry point - 5 wrappers feed one builder
key_findings.summary: Client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric' already documents that 0x012D EventStart is the c2s 'central command opcode' (carrying combat semantics via eventName/luaParams, etc.). This confirms it's also the c2s entry for ALL event-family interactions: talk requests, push triggers, notice notifications, emote events, menu confirmations, and cutscene starts. The 5 cataloged wrappers BCS-Y-0427..0431 (EventStartServerCallWrapper, EventStartRawRecordWrapper pair, EventStartRouteWrapper, EventStartFollowupWrapper, EventStartDiagnosticEmitter) all feed FUN_00776760 MapEventStartPacketBuilder (BCS-Y-0426). The c2s side of the event subsystem is FULLY ATTRIBUTED - no proposed entries needed for the emit chain.

key_findings.title: Deferred Event-Condition Scheduler is the leaf-callback firer for Talk/Push/Notice events
key_findings.summary: Set*EventCondition receivers write callback records into the 2-slot 0x54-stride callback table (BCS-S-0037), then the native Event execution scheduler walks the queue. Talk and Push leaves fire _onTalkEvent / _onTalkRequest / _onPushEvent / _onPushRequest; NoticeBlock and NoticeNonBlock have a no-op leaf slot +0x28.

key_findings.title: Cutscene playback callbacks are LuaActorImpl::vftable cancellation slots (38/39/36)
key_findings.summary: Three cutscene-related vftable slots are already cataloged: LuaActorImpl slot 38 (_onPreCutSceneCancel, FUN_00759AD0), LuaActorImpl slot 39 (_onPostCutSceneCancel, FUN_00759B40), NullActorImpl slot 36 (_onCutScenePreview, FUN_0075AD70). These fire when the user cancels a cutscene mid-playback. The cutscene START sequence is NOT in this slot range - it's via Control::CutScene class methods invoked from Lua. The asymmetry (cancel = vtable slots, start = Lua-method) suggests cutscene cancellation is a low-level system response to user input that needs to interrupt the class-level state, while start is part of normal script flow.

key_findings.title: 5/6-slot receiver classes' slot1Fn is misleading - real Receive method is at slot 2
key_findings.summary: Per docs/receiver_classes_inventory.md and the project's local memory ledger reference-receiver-vtable-layouts.md: client_receivers.json's slot1_fn field is misleading for 5-slot and 6-slot receivers. The 5-slot variants (KickClientOrderEvent, StartServerOrderEventFunction, ChangeActorSubStatStatus) have a New() factory at slot 1 and the real Receive method at slot 2. This manifest documents it by proposing distinct BCS-Y entries for the slot-2 Receive (BCS-Y-0680 KickEvent::Receive, BCS-Y-0683 StartServerOrderEvent::Receive). Note: EndClientOrderEvent is 5-slot but its slot1Fn IS the Receive (FUN_0089D180) - the factory pattern is specific to Kick/StartServerOrder. The 6-slot JobQuestCompleteTripleReceiver dispatches via 'Pattern C' instead per.
